 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by appellants/accused Nos.2 and 3 in Crime No.136/2022 registered at Nanjangud Town Police Station, Mysuru, praying to set aside the order dated 03.03.2023 passed by the learned Prl. District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru in Crl. Misc No.128/2023 and consequently to enlarge the appellants on anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Prl. District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Crime No.136/2022 of Nanjangud Town Police Station is registered on a complaint lodged by one Sinchana M NC: 2024:KHC:10824 Hadli against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Section 114, 403, 406, 420 of IPC and Section 9 of the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishment Act, 2004 (KPIDFE).

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishment Act, 2004
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is alleged in the complaint that one Shambhulinga working as a school teacher, insisted the complainant to join the chit run by him in the name of his wife i.e., accused No.1 and therefore, she became a member and paid a total sum of Rs.3,20,000/-, but in spite of maturity of the said amount, she was not paid the deposited amount and thereby she was cheated.

It is further alleged that the entire proceeds collected by various investors were invested in properties purchased in the names of the appellants, namely the father and brother of accused.No.1.
3.

The learned Sessions Judge has dismissed the petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C on the ground that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act, 2004 is invoked and therefore, the petition seeking anticipatory bail is not maintainable in view of Section 18(2) of the said Act and also relying on the decision of this Court in the case of Shreesha Sasithota Prabhakaran Vs. The State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022 dated 10.11.2022.

sentences.text: One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act is not applicable, since the definition of 'deposit', does not include the amount received by way of subscription, in respect of a chit.

5. The learned High Court Government pleader has contended that the appellants have colluded with accused No.1 and collected huge amount from many persons and cheated them by not returning the amount collected even after its maturity.
He has contended that the appellants are the father and brother of accused No.1 and they have purchased the properties in their names as well as in the names of their relatives.
He, therefore submits that the appellants are not entitled for bail as they are required for custodial interrogation.
6. Under Section 2(2)(VII) of KPIDFE Act, the definition of 'deposit' does not include the amount received by way of subscriptions in respect of chit.
The offence alleged under KPIDFE Act, is one under Section 9 of the said act i.e., any financial establishment fraudulently committing default in NC: 2024:KHC:10824 the repayment of deposit etc.
Hence, there is some force in the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants.
7. The offence alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
Accused No.1 has been granted bail in Crl.A.No.704/2023 dated 07.12.2023.
The appellants/accused Nos.2 and 3 were granted interim anticipatory bail by this Court on 21.04.2023.
It is submitted that as per the conditions stipulated therein, the appellants have appeared before the Investigating Officer and executed the bond.
8. In the above facts and circumstances, the appeal deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed.
ii) The order dated 03.03.2023 passed by the Court of the Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru in Crl.Misc No.128/2023 dismissing the petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C is set aside.
